clue.text: Bishop likely is married in sacred ritual

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
apt to do something means likely to do it
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A bishop who has wed is probably found at some holy ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here: the four pieces simply follow one another to spell BAPTISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism is a Christian sacrament, a holy rite of initiation performed with water.

clue.text: Hotel worker's infernal dance, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: infernal means of hell, so the word heard is hell
to bop is to dance, especially to pop music

explanation.surface: A hotel porter's routine pictured as a dance of the damned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to Spooner' swaps the opening H and B sounds of 'hell bop' to give 'bell hop'. The 's after worker is 'has' or 'is', a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellhop is a hotel employee who carries luggage and runs errands for guests, chiefly American usage.

clue.text: Author viciously slain outside university's piece of land

parts.note: to pen something is to author it

indicators.note: one piece placed outside another wraps around it
acting viciously means violently, so the letters are battered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A crime writer murdered on a campus plot of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author' looks like a noun but works as the verb pen; the rearranged SLAIN wraps U.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula is a stretch of land almost surrounded by water, projecting into a sea or lake.

clue.text: Federal agency to fight beer-storage option

parts.note: ICE is US Immigration and Customs Enforcement
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A government department fighting over where to keep the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is an old-fashioned name for a refrigerator or cooler, one place to keep beer cold.

clue.text: Players and ump mixed up breakfast condiment

indicators.note: something mixed up has lost its order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Baseball players and the umpire got confused at the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple syrup is poured over pancakes and waffles, a classic North American breakfast topping.

clue.text: Psychologist gives name to crappy performing ensemble

indicators.note: to give something away is to part with it, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: Carl Jung, the Swiss founder of analytical psychology
N is the abbreviation for name; this is the letter given up

explanation.surface: A psychologist lends his name to some terrible group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: JUNG loses its N to leave JUG, and the BAND is read straight from the definition's 'performing ensemble', so the clue is partly self-defining. A jug band plays on homemade instruments such as jugs and washboards.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug band is a rough folk group using makeshift instruments, so jokily it is a low-quality musical outfit.

clue.text: Potassium in coffee makes you gag

indicators.note: something put in a drink sits inside it

parts.note: joe is American slang for coffee
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: Spiking a cup of coffee with potassium would make anyone retch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' looks like choking, but it is the comedian's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag is a joke or comic line, as told by a comedian.

clue.text: Where to fill up Georgia's shoes

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, with its possessive S
pumps are a kind of shoe

explanation.surface: A question of where to find shoes worthy of a woman named Georgia, like filling her shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill up' suggests filling someone's shoes; it means refuelling a car. Gas is American for petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers fill up their tanks at gas pumps, the fuel dispensers at a filling station.

clue.text: Under any circumstances, a high

parts.note: taken as written
something tall is high

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, someone is going to get high.
explanation.definitionFit: At all is the idiom meaning in any way or under any conditions, as in 'not at all'.

clue.text: Led astray about current decrease

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
something gone astray has wandered from its course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a wind is a current of air

explanation.surface: Someone misled about the latest drop in electricity or prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' wants to be electrical; it is the moving air of a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to grow gradually smaller or fewer, to diminish.

clue.text: Thrust bar after losing ring

indicators.note: once something is lost it is no longer there, so a letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a lounge is a bar, as in a cocktail lounge
a ring is round like the letter O; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A fencer's or weightlifter's push made once the ring has come off the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust, as with a sword in fencing.

clue.text: Skip wildly to entertain a sun-baked, independent South Asian

indicators.note: a host who entertains a guest takes them inside, so one piece goes within another
doing something wildly means without order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
skin baked by the sun is tanned
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: Someone skipping about happily round a sunburnt, self-reliant traveller from South Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skip' looks like the verb of the surface, but the word itself is the raw material; only the single letter A goes inside, with the rest following.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pakistani is a person from Pakistan, a country in South Asia.

clue.text: Solo (sole) source for transfer

parts.note: Han Solo is the Star Wars smuggler, so his first name goes with Solo
Dover sole is a well-known flatfish, so its first word goes with sole

explanation.surface: A note about where a single fish or a lone performer came from before being moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word stands for the word that usually precedes it: Han before Solo, Dover before sole.
explanation.definitionFit: A handover is the act of passing control or possession to someone else, a transfer.

clue.text: In Dubuque, Lydia discussed mathematician

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: said out loud, the end of Dubuque runs into the start of Lydia

explanation.surface: A woman called Lydia from Dubuque, Iowa, talked about some famous scholar of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dubuque is a city in Iowa pronounced duh-BYOOK; spoken aloud, its last syllable runs into the start of Lydia to give the Greek geometer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek author of the Elements, the founding textbook of geometry.

clue.text: Spoiled brat, receiving tip from investor on fads, buys and sells immediately

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another
something spoiled is ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its point, here its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a rage is a craze or fad, as in 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: A spoilt kid gets a stock tip about trends and trades at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests stock advice, but it only picks out a first letter; 'all the rage' is the idiom behind the fads.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrage is to buy and sell the same asset at once in different markets to profit from a price gap.

clue.text: Removing the tip of a feather — that's a desirable job

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its end, and taking that away shortens it by one letter

parts.note: a plume is a large feather

explanation.surface: Snipping the end off a quill pen sounds like a cushy line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job or plum post is a highly sought-after position, the choicest prize.

clue.text: Extremely high-velocity way to travel around some water!

definitions.text: Extremely high-velocity way to travel around some water!

indicators.note: at the extremes means the outer ends, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of the hyphenated word
a drop is a small amount of water
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: An exclamation about some extremely fast means of getting about on water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the craft, while its pieces build the word; 'to travel around' reads only as part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydroplane is a light, fast motorboat that skims across the surface of water at high speed.

clue.text: Spot vehicle time after time in the inside track

parts.note: an advertising spot is an ad
a van is a vehicle
T is the abbreviation for time
an age is a long period of time; it comes after the other

explanation.surface: Spotting a car again and again on the inner lane of a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time after time' is read literally: one word for time placed after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the inside track is an idiom for holding a favourable position, an edge over rivals.

clue.text: Government figure's complicated topic: oil

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An official's thorny issue is the petroleum industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is an informal word for a politician or someone active in government.

clue.text: Manic Opus 1, perhaps!

indicators.note: a manic state is frenzied and disordered, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one
the indicator word itself also joins the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a composer's frantic first published work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manic' both signals the jumble and is part of it: MANIC plus OPUS plus I hold exactly the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer's first numbered work is often a set of keyboard pieces, so it may well be music for the piano.

clue.text: Medicine mostly covers mirthless wayfarer

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine, here losing its last letter
grim means humourless and stern

explanation.surface: A drug mainly masks the gloom of a sad traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'covers' means sits on top of, so the shortened medicine simply comes before the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is a traveller making a journey, typically to a sacred place.

clue.text: Lavish interior for major renter

indicators.note: the interior of a word is what lies between its ends, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters stripped away

explanation.surface: A sumptuous inside space meant for an important tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renter' looks like a tenant; here it means a company that rents things out.
explanation.definitionFit: Avis is one of the biggest car-hire companies in the world, so a leading firm that rents out vehicles.

clue.text: The first thing to do: overturn empty rule in some residences

indicators.note: to overturn a rule is to reverse it, so the phrase for that rule is read from right to left

parts.note: NO PETS is a common house rule in apartment buildings and rented homes
E marks empty on a car's fuel gauge

explanation.surface: Tenants planning their protest decide their opening move is to get the building's restrictive policy scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The rule is spelled out as a phrase, NO PETS, which turned around gives STEP ON; the fuel-gauge E then finishes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Step one is the idiom for the initial action in any procedure or plan.

clue.text: Something puzzlers work on: cheating in game

indicators.note: cheating bends the rules, so the letters do not stay in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Solvers tackling a puzzle accuse someone of cheating during play.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or riddle, the sort of thing puzzlers try to crack.

clue.text: Public display of affection — behold, it goes to the heart

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
veins are the vessels that carry blood back to the heart

explanation.surface: Kissing in public described as a sight that touches the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A love-in is a 1960s-style public gathering where people openly show their love and goodwill.

clue.text: For example, a promise on a train

parts.note: a vow is a promise
the El is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Someone making a pledge while riding the train, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single letter a, which looks like an article attached to promise.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter A is one of the vowels, so it is an instance of the category.

clue.text: Misshapen crone conceals a way to inherit military equipment

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece sits within another
something misshapen has been twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
DNA is the molecule through which traits are inherited

explanation.surface: A deformed old witch hides some heirloom that is actually army hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is the collective term for weapons, artillery and ammunition supplied to armed forces.

clue.text: Steadfast enterprise

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a description of a reliable venture; each is a separate meaning of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for solid and resolute and a noun for a business or company.

clue.text: Once again, drafting leaderless gang to circle round that thing

indicators.note: without its leader, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a crew is a gang or team of people

indicators.note: the circle goes round the pronoun, holding it inside

parts.note: to ring something is to circle it
it is the pronoun for that thing

explanation.surface: A gang without its boss is set to surround something, and the plan is being revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once again' looks like a link phrase, but it belongs to the definition: drafting once again is the answer's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewriting is the act of drafting a text again, producing a revised version of it.

clue.text: Turned onion au gratin ingredients into fertilizer

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the letters are read backwards
ingredients are what a dish contains, so the letters are inside the words

parts.note: the letters running across the end of onion, all of au, and the start of gratin

explanation.surface: A cook turning an onion gratin into something only fit for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats, collected and used as a rich manure.

clue.text: Forbes magazine's start-up: all-male holding company

indicators.note: a start is a beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: all as written plus M, the abbreviation for male
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A business magazine's new venture turns out to be a men-only parent firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbes magazine' reads as one title, but the name Forbes alone is the definition. Malcolm Forbes was the longtime publisher of the American business magazine Forbes.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm Forbes was the famous millionaire publisher, so his first name pairs with the surname in the clue.

clue.text: Pacino in a stage setting? That's irregular

indicators.note: something placed in a setting is put inside it

parts.note: a scene is the setting of a stage play
Al Pacino, the American actor

explanation.surface: An actor known for film turning up on a theatre set might seem out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' sounds like a verdict on the casting; it is the geometry term for a triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalene triangle has all three sides of different lengths, so it is irregular in shape.
